scenario: AITA For telling my Girlfriend she needs to quit whining about who eats what or I'll kick her out | Well, the title says it all, the past few weeks have both been really great and extremely infuriating. We don't live together, but we decided it would be best to stick together during these times as we have no family near as such she is staying with me as I have my own apartment and she has multiple roommates hence the choice. Well she eats more then any person I have ever known, especially considering her physical appearance, she is 5'4, petite, thin and yet she eats more than I do and I am 6'6 and a bit of a gymbro. To put it in to perspective, our food bill each week is roughly three times compared to what I usually spend alone. Yet she seems extremely selfconcious about this and as a result will act surprised when something is gone, try to blame me, states I am eating too much whenever I eat anything, essentially, she tries to deflect her eating habits and projects them on to me out of embarrassment about her eating so much I guess? The thing is, I don't care about her eating habits, she can eat whatever she wants to eat what I am done with is her constantly trying to blame me, whining about food and picking fights about it. I talked to her about it multiple times, argued with her about it multiple times but earlier today I just got so tired of another comment, this time brought on by me making a sandwhich at 2 PM when I had eaten at 10 AM I know right, horrible. So I told her that this crap was either going to stop right here and now or I'll kick her out and she can spend the coming weeks or months at her own place. She just started crying, called me horrible and locked herself in the bathroom. At this point I just dont get it anymore, am I being TA here or is she TA?

When you wear a suit and tie, you may feel more put together, professional, and prepared to take on challenges. The formal attire can signal to your brain that you're in a more serious and important mode, which can boost your confidence and self-assurance. Additionally, wearing a suit and tie can also affect how others perceive you. People may view you as more competent, trustworthy, and authoritative when you're dressed in formal attire. This can lead to a positive feedback loop, where you feel more confident because you're receiving positive cues from others. It's also worth noting that the psychological impact of wearing a suit and tie can be highly personal and subjective. Some people may feel restricted or uncomfortable in formal attire, while others may feel empowered and confident. Ultimately, it's essential to wear what makes you feel good about yourself and helps you project the image you want to convey. So, if wearing a suit and tie makes you feel confident, that's great! Own it and rock that confidence. Do you have a particular occasion or event where you feel like your suit and tie give you an extra boost of confidence?
